subject: ADR-207: a page that takes records must keep them -- and the check for the bug was written over the pages that no longer had it
body: Six pages of this kit accepted between EIGHTEEN and FORTY-SEVEN typed values and kept NONE of them: close the tab, lose the morning. One of them -- the experiment guide, the page that takes more typed values than any other here -- carried the exact `try{ localStorage.setItem(...) }catch(e){}` that KEEP was built to replace, BESIDE A CHECK WHOSE ENTIRE PURPOSE IS TO FIND THAT PATTERN, RUNNING GREEN. verify_keep has said 'no silent setItem left' since KEEP existed, and it said it about TWELVE pages: the ones already using KEEP. A RULE ENFORCED OVER THE CONVERTED SET CANNOT FIND THE UNCONVERTED ONE -- the same shape as ADR-204's consumer list and ADR-205's skipped page, a third time. Both checks are over EVERY page now. THE SIX: the experiment guide converted off its own silent setItem (saveState survives as the name every call site uses and is a debounced touch on the autosave rather than a write of its own); the cell, micro and cp benches take KEEP and the outbox; the breeding bench takes KEEP and NO outbox, because it has nothing to export; and the ecology lab is NOT converted but NAMED IN THE SUITE WITH A REASON -- it is a workbench, not a record, every box ships with a worked example, and the session files it charts come from the sheets, which keep. THE RULE IS DRIVEN: every page is opened, its value-carrying controls counted from the harness's own TYPED list, and a page at or above FOUR must mount KEEP or be named with a reason -- driven rather than read off the source, for ADR-206's reason that a check about spelling is the kind that gets edited to match the code. An exemption is a written judgement, not an absence, which is ADR-205's rule for pages that hand nothing over applied to pages that keep nothing. A RESTORED DESIGN CAME BACK WITHOUT ITS MEASUREMENT ROWS, because those rows are BUILT from what is in g-sizes and g-phases and a paint that ran before those boxes were filled drew none; the boxes go in before the renders. TWO THINGS THIS FOUND AND DID NOT FIX: the breeding bench has NO EXPORT AT ALL -- eighteen typed values across a roguing log and a yield trial and no way to get any of it off the screen -- which is an ADR-205 data trap that the rule written there MISSED, because that rule asks whether a page has an output BUTTON and this page has one that emits nothing: A SILENT BUTTON IS NOT AN OUTPUT; and the cp bench copies a soil recipe and nothing else. Both keep what you type now, which is the half that stops the loss; neither can yet hand it to anybody, which is the half that makes it data. verify_keep 221 -> 279, verify_outbox 262 -> 316, mutate_keep 23 -> 28 all killed -- and the FIRST THREE MUTANTS WRITTEN AGAINST THE NEW RULE SURVIVED, which is the finding: A RULE WITH NO VIOLATORS LEFT CANNOT SHOW THAT IT FIRES. Every page keeps now, so narrowing the rule back to the converted set changed nothing a check could see. It is run TWICE instead -- over the kit, where it must find nothing, and over a CANARY DIRECTORY built by the suite, where it must name exactly the page that deserves it and leave the one that does not: ADR-127's point about a refusal nobody has watched, arriving on a rule rather than on a gateway. The five that stand live in the SUITE rather than in keep.py, because the rule is the thing under test. AND ONE THE FULL RUN FOUND: audit_focus reported, INTERMITTENTLY, that a page had a control 'mounted after the last stamp and could not be measured' -- the ethogram once, the breeding bench once, never twice on the same page, which reads as a FLAKY INSTRUMENT rather than as the defect it is. It was the defect: KEEP's paint() wrote the whole strip with innerHTML, so its Forget button was destroyed and re-created every time the autosave changed state, which is every time it saves. A CONTROL THAT DOES NOT SURVIVE A REPAINT CANNOT BE STAMPED, ADDRESSED OR KEPT IN FOCUS ACROSS ONE. KEEP 1.1.0 -> 1.2.0: the strip is built once and only its words change. And verify_keep declares MUTATE_ROLE = 'fixture-builder', because verify_mutate rightly refuses a suite that reaches for a temp dir without saying what it is for. ONE CHECK RELAXED ON PURPOSE: the outbox suite required a page to declare TWO exports, which is a claim about how many exports a page ought to have rather than about the ledger; the cp bench makes exactly one copy and its outbox is no less true for it.
